question: Should OpenClaw intentionally make `gpt-realtime-2.1` the default OpenAI realtime voice model for users who have not set an explicit realtime model?
rationale: The code path is narrow and evidence-backed, but changing a provider default is a product and upgrade-safety choice because existing no-override installs will route to a different model after upgrade.

options.title: Accept 2.1 as default
options.body: Merge this direction after final maintainer review, relying on explicit model overrides for users who need to stay on `gpt-realtime-2`.

options.title: Keep 2 as default
options.body: Leave `gpt-realtime-2` as the default and document `gpt-realtime-2.1` as an explicit opt-in model until maintainers want the upgrade train to move.

options.title: Require broader upgrade proof
options.body: Hold the PR until fresh-install and upgrade proof covers the no-override default path plus explicit `gpt-realtime-2` override behavior.

recommendation.title: Accept 2.1 as default
recommendation.body: Merge this direction after final maintainer review, relying on explicit model overrides for users who need to stay on `gpt-realtime-2`.
